extracted.intended_audience: covered health programs and activities (health care providers, payers, insurers), compliance officers, legal counsel, and stakeholders commenting on or implementing HHS Section 1557 rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and enforceable standards under HHS's final rule implementing section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, focused on nondiscrimination obligations in health programs and activities (e.g., sex discrimination, LEP language access). For covered entities to understand prohibited conduct and language-access duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exhaustive treatment of 'sex' discrimination (§92.101(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to define 'sex' in the rule but provides a non-exhaustive list of what constitutes discrimination on the basis of sex at §92.101(a)(2), and will interpret section 1557's protections on the basis of sex consistent with applicable case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supreme Court in Bostock did not define 'sex'; OCR will not attempt a single definition here but will rely on the enumerated examples in §92.101(a)(2) and case law. OCR also notes that Bostock proceeded on the assumption of biological distinctions but that its reasoning did not hinge on a narrow binary definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on sex characteristics (including intersex traits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sex characteristics, including intersex variations, is a prohibited form of sex discrimination because discrimination based on anatomical or physiological sex characteristics is inherently sex-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR retains reference to 'sex characteristics' (including intersex traits) in §92.101(a)(2). Commenters' requests to remove or avoid the term were declined; OCR treats discrimination based on intersex traits as sex discrimination and may rely on evidence (e.g., provider refusals) showing disparate treatment to enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of pregnancy or related conditions as protected bases
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule includes 'pregnancy or related conditions' within sex discrimination protections at §92.101(a)(2), consistent with longstanding Title IX interpretation that pregnancy-based discrimination is sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection may include discrimination experienced throughout pregnancy, labor and delivery, and the postpartum period. OCR decided to keep 'pregnancy or related conditions' in §92.101(a)(2) rather than create a separate section, and cross-references further discussion at §92.208.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy-related protections encompass termination of pregnancy (interpretive approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR recognizes that protections for 'pregnancy or related conditions' include termination of pregnancy but declines to explicitly include or exclude specific examples in §92.101(a)(2); interpretation will follow applicable case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will evaluate claims case-by-case. A covered provider's general refusal to provide abortions (e.g., for religious or conscience reasons) is not itself a violation; however, denial of unrelated medical care because a patient had a prior abortion or discrimination against an individual based on actual or perceived prior abortions could violate section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscience and federal/state abortion laws preserved (no forcing of abortion provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the ACA or section 1557 affects Federal conscience protections or State laws regarding abortion coverage, funding, or procedural requirements; a covered provider's decision not to provide abortions does not itself constitute section 1557 discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR cites 42 U.S.C. 18023(c)(2)(A) and 42 U.S.C. 18023(c)(1) to emphasize that conscience protections and state abortion law regimes remain in force; enforcement focuses on discrimination on protected grounds, not on forcing providers to offer particular services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections apply across reproductive health and fertility care
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 protects individuals against prohibited discrimination regardless of the type of care sought, including fertility care, maternity care, and other reproductive health care, throughout preconception, pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR says it is unnecessary to list every form of health care in the rule; whether discrimination occurred in provision or coverage of assistive reproductive technology (e.g., IVF) is fact-specific, but categorical denial of services to a protected class (e.g., same-sex couples) may violate section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for sexual orientation and gender identity as forms of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity is treated as prohibited sex discrimination under section 1557; OCR supports explicit inclusion of these bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes varied terminology and declines to narrowly define 'gender identity' or 'transgender status', but will investigate discrimination based on having a gender identity different from sex assigned at birth as discrimination on the basis of gender identity. Bostock reasoning supports inclusion of transgender and gender nonconforming individuals within sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: No regulatory definition for 'gender identity' or 'transgender status' (interpretive approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to provide regulatory definitions of 'gender identity' or 'transgender status' and will investigate claims based on the substance of the allegation rather than reliance on a particular label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will evaluate discrimination claims based on whether an individual is discriminated against for having a gender identity different from their sex assigned at birth, regardless of the specific term the individual uses to describe themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of prohibitions from other civil-rights statutes into §92.101(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR proposes explicitly incorporating prohibitions on discrimination found in Title VI, Section 504, Title IX, and the Age Act into §92.101(b) to help health entities unfamiliar with those standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters expressed concern about importing outdated or conflicting provisions (e.g., 45 CFR 84.23(c) applying UFAS); OCR notes facility accessibility is addressed separately at §92.203 and directs readers there rather than importing every historic standard verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of Age Act implementing regulation provisions by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule adopts by reference the Age Act implementing regulation provisions at 45 CFR part 91 (subpart B), which recognize some statutorily permissive age distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach preserves treatment of age distinctions and the Age Act's explicit recognition that some age distinctions may be necessary for program operation or statutory objectives; commenters' requests to restore prior clarifications were considered in light of 45 CFR part 91.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline to import certain prior provisions (e.g., site location) or piecemeal legal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to include some prior-rule provisions (such as a site location provision from the 2016 Rule) or to import a patchwork of legal standards and burdens from other statutory contexts; instead OCR preserves longstanding treatments consistent with case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will apply statutory text and case law to enforcement and will not automatically graft all prior rule provisions into this rule where they would create doctrinal conflict or unnecessary complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful access standard for individuals with limited English proficiency (§92.201(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities 'must take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to each limited English proficient individual eligible to be served or likely to be directly affected by its health programs and activities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised earlier wording ('likely to be directly affected' vs 'likely to be encountered') to clarify applicability and reduce burden. This obligation also applies to companions with LEP. 'Reasonable steps' and 'meaningful access' are left undefined in the regulation but reflect longstanding Title VI requirements; OCR may issue further guidance and refers to HHS LEP Guidance and HHS reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language assistance services requirements (free, accurate, timely, protect privacy) (§92.201(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Required language assistance services must be provided free of charge, be accurate and timely, and protect the privacy and independent decision-making ability of an individual with LEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inaccurate or incomplete translations or late interpretation may violate the accuracy and timeliness standards and could constitute denial of meaningful access. OCR addresses accuracy concerns by requiring qualified interpreters and translators in §92.201(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified interpreter and translator requirement (§92.201(c)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpreter services are required, a covered entity must offer a qualified interpreter; when translation services are required, a covered entity must use a qualified translator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR ties qualification to definitions in §92.4 and expects entities to ensure competency. Use of unqualified persons can lead to inaccurate communications that violate the meaningful access obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine translation rules and human review requirement (§92.201(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity that uses machine translation must have translated materials reviewed by a qualified human translator when the underlying text is critical to rights/benefits/meaningful access, when accuracy is essential, or when source materials contain complex, non-literal, or technical language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes some limited exigent uses of machine translation (e.g., urgent EMS care) but requires subsequent human review 'as soon as practicable.' OCR recommends warning patients when MT is used in non-critical circumstances and defines machine translation in §92.4 to include automated speech-to-text translations. OCR declined to allow unreviewed machine translation generally because of error risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's evaluation factors for compliance (§92.201(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating compliance, the Director will give substantial weight to the nature and importance of the health program or activity and the particular communication at issue, and will take into account other relevant factors such as the effectiveness of a covered entity's written language access procedures implemented under §92.8(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR moved away from a rigid 'four-factor analysis' and emphasizes context-specific review, including urgency and importance of the service, geographic and temporal variables for timeliness, and written procedures the entity has adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of certain persons for language assistance (§92.201(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are prohibited from requiring individuals with LEP to provide or pay for their own interpreters; reliance on minors to interpret is prohibited except temporarily in emergencies with imminent threat and no qualified interpreter available; reliance on staff other than qualified interpreters/translators or qualified bilingual/multilingual staff to communicate directly with LEP individuals is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions protect privacy and accuracy and prevent placing cost or burden on LEP individuals. Limited exceptions (e.g., emergency temporary use of a minor) are narrowly construed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for video remote interpreting (VRI) and audio remote interpreting (§92.201(f)-(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule sets forth standards for VRI and for audio remote interpreting services when used to provide language assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although detailed standards are in the regulatory text, OCR highlights the need for such remote interpreting to meet accuracy, timeliness, privacy, and qualification requirements and to be evaluated in context for adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No compulsion for LEP individuals to accept assistance (§92.201(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require an individual with LEP to accept language assistance services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities must offer appropriate services, but provision requires consent; choice must be respected while ensuring the individual is offered sufficient means for meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companions with LEP are covered by language access obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities' language access obligations apply to companions (as defined in §92.4) who are directly affected by health programs and activities by virtue of their relationship to the person receiving care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will add clarifying parenthetical to §92.201(a) to explicitly include companions (e.g., a parent with LEP whose minor child is treated or a spouse assisting with post-operative care). This aligns with §92.202 effective-communication protections for companions with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and context-specific standard for language assistance (no fixed metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to define 'timeliness' with fixed time/distance/wait time metrics; timeliness depends on variables including urgency, geographic location, and hour of day, and language assistance should avoid effective denial or undue delay of rights, benefits, or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating complaints, OCR will consider the context and urgency (e.g., emergency care). Entities should refer to HHS LEP Guidance for examples and best practices rather than relying on a single numerical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural competency and dialect sensitivity in language services (policy expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural competency is essential for equitable language access; accurate interpretation often requires awareness of dialect, regionalism, and cultural nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR agrees community-based or community-origin interpreters can improve accuracy and trust, but declines to mandate that interpreters/translators be from the community. Covered entities may determine hiring/contracting processes as long as personnel meet §92.4 qualification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy obligations: errors can violate meaningful access
rubrics_metrics.description: Inaccurate or incomplete translations/interpretations can violate the accuracy standard and the overarching requirement to take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR emphasizes use of qualified interpreters/translators and human review of machine translation for critical communications; examples of translation errors harming access are cited to justify strict accuracy obligations.
